title: Finite and countable Postnikov systems and their morphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] and let $X_\bullet$ be a complex indexed by $\mathbf N$ with arrows $d_{r+1}:X_{r+1}\to X_r$. For $N\in\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$ a normalized Postnikov system through $N$ consists of objects $Y_r$ and maps $a_r:Y_r\to X_r$ for $0\le r\le N$, an equality $Y_0=X_0$ identifying $a_0$ with the identity, and maps $b_{r+1}:X_{r+1}\to Y_r$, $c_{r+1}:Y_r\to Y_{r+1}[1]$ for $r+1\le N$, such that $Y_{r+1}\xrightarrow{a_{r+1}}X_{r+1}\xrightarrow{b_{r+1}}Y_r\xrightarrow{c_{r+1}}Y_{r+1}[1]$ is distinguished and $a_r b_{r+1}=d_{r+1}$. Restriction to $M\le N$ retains these objects and maps. For a map of complexes $u:X_\bullet\to X'_\bullet$, a map of systems over $u$ is a family $g_r:Y_r\to Y'_r$, with $g_0=u_0$ under the degree-zero equalities, satisfying all three triangle squares $a'_rg_r=u_ra_r$, $b'_ru_r=g_{r-1}b_r$, $g_r[1]c_r=c'_rg_{r-1}$ for $1\le r\le N$. Its restriction retains the same components. The connecting sequence has vertices $Y_r[r]$ and arrows $c_{r+1}[r]:Y_r[r]\to Y_{r+1}[r+1]$, using the canonical shift-composition identification.
